references.text: The Ishmaelites are mentioned as traders, which explains why the Midianites are also called Ishmaelites in Judges 8:24, since these groups had overlapping identities as nomadic merchants.
Ishmael, the patriarch of the Ishmaelites, and his descendants are mentioned here, providing background for the people group referred to in Judges 8:24.
Gold rings (nose rings) were given as gifts, similar to the gold rings Gideon requested from the spoils.
Aaron collected gold rings from the people to make the golden calf, just as Gideon collected gold rings to make an ephod.
The result of collecting the gold rings is mentioned here, where Gideon made an ephod that became a snare for Israel.
The war spoils from the Midianites included gold jewelry that was given as an offering to the Lord, similar to the situation in Judges 8.
